items.title: Quiz Q#251 · Ford Madox Ford
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ford Madox Ford
items.stem: In which work by Ford Madox Ford does the character John Dowell (The American narrator, whose account the reader cannot fully trust) appear?
items.explanation: John Dowell (The American narrator, whose account the reader cannot fully trust) is a central character in Ford Madox Ford's The Good Soldier.

items.title: Quiz Q#252 · Ford Madox Ford
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ford Madox Ford
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Having a rattling good time."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ford Madox Ford's The Good Soldier.

items.title: Quiz Q#253 · Ford Madox Ford
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ford Madox Ford
items.stem: Which modernist novel employs the famously unreliable American narrator John Dowell, bears the subtitle 'A Tale of Passion', and opens with the line: 'This is the saddest story I have ever heard'?
items.explanation: Ford Madox Ford's The Good Soldier (1915) is subtitled 'A Tale of Passion' and features the narration of John Dowell unraveling the tragic lives of the Ashburnhams and the Dowells.

items.title: Quiz Q#254 · Ford Madox Ford
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ford Madox Ford
items.stem: In which work by Ford Madox Ford does the character Christopher Tietjens (A brilliant old fashioned Englishman, called the last Tory (an old conservative)) appear?
items.explanation: Christopher Tietjens (A brilliant old fashioned Englishman, called the last Tory (an old conservative)) is a central character in Ford Madox Ford's Parade’s End.

items.title: Quiz Q#255 · Ford Madox Ford
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ford Madox Ford
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "This is what the late war was like."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ford Madox Ford's Parade’s End.

items.title: Quiz Q#256 · Ford Madox Ford
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ford Madox Ford
items.stem: Which monumental modernist tetralogy by Ford Madox Ford—comprising Some Do Not..., No More Parades, A Man Could Stand Up—, and Last Post—chronicles the psychological impact of World War I on the conservative statistician Christopher Tietjens?
items.explanation: Parade's End (1924–1928) is Ford Madox Ford's tetralogy documenting English society and the trench experience through Christopher Tietjens, often called 'the last Tory'.

items.title: Quiz Q#257 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: In which work by E. M. Forster does the character Lilia Herriton (English widow who marries Gino in Monteriano and dies in childbirth) appear?
items.explanation: Lilia Herriton (English widow who marries Gino in Monteriano and dies in childbirth) is a central character in E. M. Forster's Where Angels Fear to Tread.

items.title: Quiz Q#258 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Where angels fear to tread."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in E. M. Forster's Where Angels Fear to Tread.

items.title: Quiz Q#259 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: Which early novel by E. M. Forster depicts the clash between conventional English suburban values and passionate Italian culture following the impulsive marriage of the widow Lilia Herriton to Gino Carella in Monteriano?
items.explanation: E. M. Forster's Where Angels Fear to Tread (1905) satirizes English provincialism when the Herritons attempt to rescue Lilia's baby from Italy.

items.title: Quiz Q#260 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: In which work by E. M. Forster does the character Lucy Honeychurch (Young Englishwoman who learns to choose George over Cecil) appear?
items.explanation: Lucy Honeychurch (Young Englishwoman who learns to choose George over Cecil) is a central character in E. M. Forster's A Room with a View.

items.title: Quiz Q#261 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Women like looking at a view; men don't."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in E. M. Forster's A Room with a View.

items.title: Quiz Q#262 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: Which romantic comedy of manners by E. M. Forster follows Lucy Honeychurch's struggle between the rigid propriety of Cecil Vyse and the passionate spontaneity of George Emerson after their visit to Florence?
items.explanation: A Room with a View (1908) contrasts Edwardian emotional restraint with Italian openness through Lucy Honeychurch's moral and romantic awakening.

items.title: Quiz Q#263 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: In which work by E. M. Forster does the character Margaret Schlegel (Thoughtful sister who marries Henry and finally holds the house) appear?
items.explanation: Margaret Schlegel (Thoughtful sister who marries Henry and finally holds the house) is a central character in E. M. Forster's Howards End.

items.title: Quiz Q#264 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: Which novel by E. M. Forster famously carries the epigraph 'Only connect...', exploring the social and spiritual conditions of England through the intellectual Schlegels, the capitalist Wilcoxes, and the impoverished Basts?
items.explanation: Howards End (1910) centers on Margaret Schlegel, Ruth Wilcox, and the inheritance of the country home Howards End, symbolizing the future of England.

items.title: Quiz Q#265 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: In which work by E. M. Forster does the character Dr Aziz (Muslim Indian doctor accused after the cave visit) appear?
items.explanation: Dr Aziz (Muslim Indian doctor accused after the cave visit) is a central character in E. M. Forster's A Passage to India.

items.title: Quiz Q#266 · E. M. Forster
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · E. M. Forster
items.stem: Which landmark 1924 novel by E. M. Forster is structured in three parts titled 'Mosque', 'Caves', and 'Temple', examining the tragic misunderstandings between the British and Indians centered on the mysterious Marabar Caves?
items.explanation: A Passage to India (1924) dramatizes the racial and political impasse of British rule in India through the friendship of Dr. Aziz and Cyril Fielding.

items.title: Quiz Q#267 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: In which work by Sarojini Naidu does the character The palanquin bearers (Men who carry a bride and sing as they walk) appear?
items.explanation: The palanquin bearers (Men who carry a bride and sing as they walk) is a central character in Sarojini Naidu's The Golden Threshold.

items.title: Quiz Q#268 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Lightly, O lightly we bear her along."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Sarojini Naidu's The Golden Threshold.

items.title: Quiz Q#269 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: Which debut poetry collection by Sarojini Naidu, introduced by Arthur Symons in 1905, contains lyrical poems such as 'Palanquin-Bearers' and 'Coromandel Fishers'?
items.explanation: The Golden Threshold (1905) established Sarojini Naidu as the 'Nightingale of India' (Bharat Kokila) with its rich Indian imagery and musical lyricism.

items.title: Quiz Q#270 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: In which work by Sarojini Naidu does the character The bangle sellers (Sellers who carry shining bangles to the temple fair) appear?
items.explanation: The bangle sellers (Sellers who carry shining bangles to the temple fair) is a central character in Sarojini Naidu's The Bird of Time.

items.title: Quiz Q#271 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Bangle sellers are we who bear."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Sarojini Naidu's The Bird of Time.

items.title: Quiz Q#272 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: Which poetry collection by Sarojini Naidu, published in 1912 with an introduction by Edmund Gosse, includes verses on folk life, death, and nature, subtitled 'Songs of Life, Death and the Spring'?
items.explanation: The Bird of Time (1912) includes some of Naidu's most mature lyrics on Indian spiritual and cultural traditions.

items.title: Quiz Q#273 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: In which work by Sarojini Naidu does the character Mother India (The speaking voice of The Gift of India, mourning sons who died abroad) appear?
items.explanation: Mother India (The speaking voice of The Gift of India, mourning sons who died abroad) is a central character in Sarojini Naidu's The Broken Wing.

items.title: Quiz Q#274 · Sarojini Naidu
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Sarojini Naidu
items.stem: Which 1917 collection of poetry by Sarojini Naidu carries the subtitle 'Songs of Love, Death and Destiny', featuring poignant patriotic and spiritual verses composed during the height of the national freedom struggle?
items.explanation: The Broken Wing (1917) reflects Naidu's deepening involvement in the Indian nationalist movement alongside Gandhi.

items.title: Quiz Q#275 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character Rachel Vinrace (A sheltered young English woman and talented pianist) appear?
items.explanation: Rachel Vinrace (A sheltered young English woman and talented pianist) is a central character in Virginia Woolf's The Voyage Out.

items.title: Quiz Q#276 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: Which debut novel by Virginia Woolf depicts Rachel Vinrace's voyage aboard the Euphrosyne to South America, charting her emotional and artistic awakening before her tragic, sudden death from fever?
items.explanation: Virginia Woolf's The Voyage Out (1915) marks her transition from traditional Victorian narrative toward the psychological exploration of female selfhood.

items.title: Quiz Q#277 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character Clarissa Dalloway (A fifty-one-year-old upper-class hostess giving an evening party) appear?
items.explanation: Clarissa Dalloway (A fifty-one-year-old upper-class hostess giving an evening party) is a central character in Virginia Woolf's Mrs Dalloway.

items.title: Quiz Q#278 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "She would buy the flowers herself."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Virginia Woolf's Mrs Dalloway.

items.stem:
Which of the following works by Virginia Woolf matches this literary feature / description?

items.explanation: The exact first publication date is 14 May 1925 by Hogarth Press. Working title was The Hours. describes Mrs Dalloway (1925) by Virginia Woolf.

items.title: Quiz Q#280 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character The Common Reader (An everyday book lover who reads for private enjoyment without scholarly bias) appear?
items.explanation: The Common Reader (An everyday book lover who reads for private enjoyment without scholarly bias) is a central character in Virginia Woolf's The Common Reader.

items.title: Quiz Q#281 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem:
Which of the following works by Virginia Woolf matches this literary feature / description?
"First series published on 23 April 1925; second series published in October 1932 by Hogarth Press."
items.explanation: First series published on 23 April 1925; second series published in October 1932 by Hogarth Press. describes The Common Reader (1925 (First Series); 1932 (Second Series)) by Virginia Woolf.

items.title: Quiz Q#282 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character Mrs. Ramsay (A warm and beautiful mother who brings family and guests together) appear?
items.explanation: Mrs. Ramsay (A warm and beautiful mother who brings family and guests together) is a central character in Virginia Woolf's To the Lighthouse.

items.title: Quiz Q#283 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "I have had my vision."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Virginia Woolf's To the Lighthouse.

items.title: Quiz Q#284 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem:
Which of the following works by Virginia Woolf matches this literary feature / description?
"The exact first publication date is 5 May 1927 by Hogarth Press."
items.explanation: The exact first publication date is 5 May 1927 by Hogarth Press. describes To the Lighthouse (1927) by Virginia Woolf.

items.title: Quiz Q#285 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character Orlando (An immortal aristocrat and poet who changes sex from male to female) appear?
items.explanation: Orlando (An immortal aristocrat and poet who changes sex from male to female) is a central character in Virginia Woolf's Orlando.

items.title: Quiz Q#286 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: Which groundbreaking biographical novel by Virginia Woolf, dedicated to Vita Sackville-West, spans three hundred years of history as its protagonist mysteriously transforms from a male Elizabethan nobleman to a modern 20th-century woman writer?
items.explanation: Orlando (1928) satirizes conventional biography and explores gender fluidity and historical consciousness across four centuries.

items.title: Quiz Q#287 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character Mary Beton / Mary Seton / Mary Carmichael (The narrator persona (a voice used by an author)) appear?
items.explanation: Mary Beton / Mary Seton / Mary Carmichael (The narrator persona (a voice used by an author)) is a central character in Virginia Woolf's A Room of One’s Own.

items.title: Quiz Q#288 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem:
Which of the following works by Virginia Woolf matches this literary feature / description?
"The book was published on 24 October 1929 by Hogarth Press, based on 1928 lectures."
items.explanation: The book was published on 24 October 1929 by Hogarth Press, based on 1928 lectures. describes A Room of One’s Own (1929) by Virginia Woolf.

items.title: Quiz Q#289 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character Bernard (A phrasemaker and storyteller who provides the final summary) appear?
items.explanation: Bernard (A phrasemaker and storyteller who provides the final summary) is a central character in Virginia Woolf's The Waves.

items.title: Quiz Q#290 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "The waves broke on the shore."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Virginia Woolf's The Waves.

items.title: Quiz Q#291 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: Which lyric masterpiece by Virginia Woolf consists of six soliloquizing voices—Bernard, Susan, Rhoda, Neville, Jinny, and Louis—interspersed with poetic descriptions of coastal seascapes from sunrise to sunset?
items.explanation: The Waves (1931) is Woolf's most radical 'play-poem', replacing conventional plot with rhythmic internal monologues tracing six lives from childhood to old age.

items.title: Quiz Q#292 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: In which work by Virginia Woolf does the character 'the protagonist' appear?
items.explanation: the protagonist is a central character in Virginia Woolf's Three Guineas (1938).

items.title: Quiz Q#293 · Virginia Woolf
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Virginia Woolf
items.stem: Which polemical anti-war feminist essay by Virginia Woolf, published in 1938, connects patriarchal oppression in the domestic sphere with the rise of fascism in Europe?
items.explanation: Three Guineas (1938) responds to a gentleman's letter asking how to prevent war by advocating women's education, economic independence, and the 'Outsiders' Society'.

items.title: Quiz Q#294 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: In which work by D. H. Lawrence does the character Paul Morel (The son who cannot easily separate love from his mother) appear?
items.explanation: Paul Morel (The son who cannot easily separate love from his mother) is a central character in D. H. Lawrence's Sons and Lovers.

items.title: Quiz Q#295 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "The Bottoms succeeded to Hell Row."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in D. H. Lawrence's Sons and Lovers.

items.title: Quiz Q#296 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Which semi-autobiographical novel by D. H. Lawrence depicts the coal-mining town of Bestwood and explores Paul Morel's Oedipal devotion to his mother Gertrude alongside his troubled relationships with Miriam Leivers and Clara Dawes?
items.explanation: Sons and Lovers (1913) is Lawrence's breakthrough novel examining maternal possessiveness and working-class emotional conflict.

items.title: Quiz Q#297 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: In which work by D. H. Lawrence does the character Tom Brangwen (The Marsh farmer who marries Lydia) appear?
items.explanation: Tom Brangwen (The Marsh farmer who marries Lydia) is a central character in D. H. Lawrence's The Rainbow.

items.title: Quiz Q#298 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "The Brangwens had lived for generations"?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in D. H. Lawrence's The Rainbow.

items.title: Quiz Q#299 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Which ambitious generational novel by D. H. Lawrence traces three generations of the Brangwen dynasty at Marsh Farm, culminating in Ursula Brangwen's quest for individual and sexual independence?
items.explanation: The Rainbow (1915) challenged Victorian morality through its depiction of female autonomy and was prosecuted and banned for obscenity shortly after its release.

items.title: Quiz Q#300 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: In which work by D. H. Lawrence does the character Ursula Brangwen (The sister who pairs with Birkin) appear?
items.explanation: Ursula Brangwen (The sister who pairs with Birkin) is a central character in D. H. Lawrence's Women in Love.

items.title: Quiz Q#301 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Which profound post-WWI novel by D. H. Lawrence continues the story of Ursula and Gudrun Brangwen, contrasting Ursula's life-affirming union with Rupert Birkin against Gudrun's destructive relationship with the industrialist Gerald Crich?
items.explanation: Women in Love (1920) critiques modern mechanical civilization, featuring famous scenes like Birkin and Gerald's wrestling match and Gerald's death in the Alpine snow.

items.title: Quiz Q#302 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: In which work by D. H. Lawrence does the character 'the protagonist' appear?
items.explanation: the protagonist is a central character in D. H. Lawrence's Lady Chatterley’s Lover (1928).

items.title: Quiz Q#303 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Ours is essentially a tragic age"?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in D. H. Lawrence's Lady Chatterley’s Lover.

items.title: Quiz Q#304 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem:
Which of the following works by D. H. Lawrence matches this literary feature / description?
"The full text was privately printed in Florence in 1928. Lawrence was still alive."
items.explanation: The full text was privately printed in Florence in 1928. Lawrence was still alive. describes Lady Chatterley’s Lover (1928) by D. H. Lawrence.

items.title: Quiz Q#305 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: In which work by D. H. Lawrence does the character Constance Chatterley (The same heroine as in the 1928 novel) appear?
items.explanation: Constance Chatterley (The same heroine as in the 1928 novel) is a central character in D. H. Lawrence's UK unexpurgated edition.

items.title: Quiz Q#306 · D. H. Lawrence
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · D. H. Lawrence
items.stem: Which landmark 1960 trial at the Old Bailey under the Obscene Publications Act 1959 resulted in Penguin Books being acquitted for publishing the complete, uncensored text of D. H. Lawrence's Lady Chatterley's Lover?
items.explanation: The 1960 Penguin trial was a watershed moment in British literary and legal history, vindicating Lawrence's uncensored novel with testimony from E. M. Forster and Richard Hoggart.

items.title: Quiz Q#307 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound

items.explanation: Cino (A wandering singer, one of the early masks in the book) is a central character in Ezra Pound's A Lume Spento.

items.title: Quiz Q#308 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "With tapers quenched."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ezra Pound's A Lume Spento.

items.title: Quiz Q#309 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Which debut poetry collection by Ezra Pound, self-published in Venice in 1908 and dedicated to his friend William Brooke Smith, introduced his early Browning-inspired dramatic lyrics?
items.explanation: A Lume Spento (1908) launched Ezra Pound's career with poems rooted in Provençal troubadour lyricism, Italian verse, and Pre-Raphaelite aestheticism.

items.title: Quiz Q#310 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: In which work by Ezra Pound does the character The personae (Historical and invented speakers whom Pound uses as masks) appear?
items.explanation: The personae (Historical and invented speakers whom Pound uses as masks) is a central character in Ezra Pound's Personae.

items.title: Quiz Q#311 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Make strong old dreams."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ezra Pound's Personae.

items.title: Quiz Q#312 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Which 1909 London collection of poems by Ezra Pound established his reputation as a pioneering new voice through dramatic masks and historical voices of Provençal and Latin poets?
items.explanation: Personae (1909) demonstrated Pound's mastery of the poetic persona, praised by Edward Thomas and W. B. Yeats.

items.title: Quiz Q#313 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: In which work by Ezra Pound does the character E. P. (The poet judged in the opening ode, a mask close to Pound) appear?
items.explanation: E. P. (The poet judged in the opening ode, a mask close to Pound) is a central character in Ezra Pound's Hugh Selwyn Mauberley.

items.title: Quiz Q#314 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "For a botched civilisation."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ezra Pound's Hugh Selwyn Mauberley.

items.title: Quiz Q#315 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Which 1920 poetic sequence by Ezra Pound critiques the philistine commercialism of post-war British society and laments the slaughter of World War I fought 'for an old bitch gone in the teeth, / For a botched civilization'?
items.explanation: Hugh Selwyn Mauberley (1920) is Pound's farewell to London, contrasting the aesthetic ideals of 'E.P.' and Mauberley against modern cultural decay.

items.title: Quiz Q#316 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: In which work by Ezra Pound does the character 'the protagonist' appear?
items.explanation: the protagonist is a central character in Ezra Pound's The Cantos (1925).

items.title: Quiz Q#317 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "And then went down to the ship."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Ezra Pound's The Cantos.

items.title: Quiz Q#318 · Ezra Pound
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Ezra Pound
items.stem: Which monumental, unfinished modernist epic poem by Ezra Pound, spanning over 116 cantos and several decades, incorporates Chinese ideograms, economics, Greek myth, and Renaissance Italian history?
items.explanation: The Cantos (1925–1969) is Pound's vast lifelong 'poem including history', beginning with Odysseus's voyage to the underworld in Canto I.

items.title: Quiz Q#319 · Katherine Mansfield

items.title: Quiz Q#320 · Katherine Mansfield
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Katherine Mansfield
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Everything here's filthy."?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Katherine Mansfield's In a German Pension.

items.title: Quiz Q#321 · Katherine Mansfield

options: The Garden Party and Other Stories
items.explanation: In a German Pension (1911) launched Katherine Mansfield's literary career with sharp, cynical character studies of European bourgeois society.

items.title: Quiz Q#322 · Katherine Mansfield
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Katherine Mansfield
items.stem: In which work by Katherine Mansfield does the character Bertha Young (The hostess whose bliss hides a blind spot in her marriage) appear?
options: The Garden Party and Other Stories
items.explanation: Bertha Young (The hostess whose bliss hides a blind spot in her marriage) is a central character in Katherine Mansfield's “Bliss”.

items.title: Quiz Q#323 · Katherine Mansfield
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Katherine Mansfield
items.stem: Who is the author of the work containing the following famous line: "Oh, what is going to happen now?"?
items.explanation: This famous line appears in Katherine Mansfield's “Bliss”.

items.title: Quiz Q#324 · Katherine Mansfield
items.meta: The Modernist & Inter-War Era · Katherine Mansfield
